headline: US markets closed today for Thanksgiving; Friday closes at 1 p.m. ET. Wednesday: Dow +0.3%, S&P 500 -0.3%, Nasdaq -0.6% after an intraday chip rout. Core PCE 3.3%, a Dec 9 Fed hike is about fully priced. Oil up ~2%. US proposed new tariffs on 14 partners from January 2027.

sectors.why: No clear sector news. October core PCE came in at 3.3%, a bit hot, and a December 9 Fed hike is now about fully priced, a mild headwind but already expected.
No specific US telecom news. The 10-year yield eased to about 4.85% Wednesday, a small help for dividend payers, but more Fed hikes are being discussed for next year.
A December Fed hike is about fully priced after hot core PCE, keeping loan costs high, and the new tariff proposal names Chinese appliances and Japanese and Korean cars.
Defensive names held up as money left chips, but no clear month-long driver. Tariffs proposed on 14 partners would not start before January 2027.
Consumer spending rose 0.3% in October and jobless claims stayed low at 189,000, a plus, but hot inflation and a near-certain Fed hike limit the upside.
The proposed tariffs on 14 trading partners could raise import costs, but they start no earlier than January 2027 and rates are still being argued. No clear direction yet.
The chip sell-off continued: Nvidia fell 3.9% and Micron 4.5%, and the Nasdaq briefly fell about 4.6% intraday, near bear-market territory. Asian chip makers dropped sharply too.
Oil rose about 2-2.5% Wednesday, with WTI near $84 and Brent around $91 or higher. A modest tailwind if prices hold, but oil swings fast.
Financials and small caps rose Wednesday as money rotated out of tech. A December hike can help bank margins but weighs on borrowing, so no clear direction.
No clear sector-wide news since the last close. Rates and inflation are the main background factors.
No clear sector-wide news. Health care slipped Wednesday after leading on Tuesday, with no single driver.
Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% growth, a plus for activity, but higher rates and tariff uncertainty offset it.
No clear news for this group.
The US proposed new tariffs on 14 partners aimed at excess factory capacity, naming Chinese steel and aluminum, which tends to help US producers. Effective no earlier than January 2027.
Tariffs on Chinese overcapacity could help some US makers, but higher oil raises input costs. No clear direction.
Strong GDP and possible protection from the new tariff proposal help, but costlier imported parts and a December Fed hike work the other way.
The new tariff proposal covers big sourcing countries such as China, Vietnam, Cambodia and Bangladesh, and inflation is running hot, squeezing margins and shoppers into 2027.
Worries about AI spending hit big tech again: Amazon fell about 3% and Alphabet about 2%, while Meta rose about 3%. Mixed, but the AI trade is under pressure.
Higher oil prices raise fuel costs, but holiday travel and strong GDP support demand. No clear direction.
The 10-year yield eased to about 4.85%, a small help, but a December hike and talk of more hikes in 2027 keep rate pressure on.

avoid.NVDA: Down about 27% in November with ongoing investigations into the CEO's actions and export controls, per two reports; very volatile for a month-long hold.
